headline: Leafs’ Marchenko exits game vs. Flames with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto's Marchenko left the game against Calgary with a lower-body injury, suffered in a collision with Flames forward Yegor Sharangovich. No further detail on his status was given.

For the Leafs, the numbers say the standing flatters them. TOR is 7-4-2, yet it has controlled only 47.6% of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season. Its results run 8.7 goals ahead of what its chances predict, and goalies have saved 5.5 more than expected. That cushion makes a lineup hit easier to absorb in the standings but harder to ignore on the ice.

Sharangovich, the other party in the collision, is a steady piece for CGY. He has 4 points in 10 games and plays 16.32 minutes a night, with 2.38 expected goals against 2 actual, so his scoring is close to what his chances warrant. Calgary controls 50.47% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share rises 4.22 points when he plays, even as the Flames sit 4-6-0.
